chapter.v: Job replied,

“Yes, I
know all that! But how can anyone be right before God?

If you
wanted to argue with God, God could ask a thousand questions that no one could answer.

God is
so wise and so powerful that no one could challenge him and win.

God moves
the mountains suddenly; he overturns them in his anger.

He shakes
the earth, making its foundations quake.

He is
the one who can command the sun not to rise and the stars not to shine.

He alone
is the one who stretches out the heavens and walks on the waves of the sea.

He made
the constellations of the Bear, Orion, the Pleiades, and the stars of the southern sky.

He is
the one who does incredible things that are beyond our understanding, marvelous things that are uncountable.

But when
he passes by me, I don't see him; when he moves on, he is invisible to me.

If he
takes away, who can prevent him? Who is going to ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

God does
not restrain his anger; he crushes Rahab's helpers underfoot.

So how
much less could I answer God, or choose my words to argue with him!

Even though
I'm right, I can't answer him. I must plead for mercy from my judge.

Even if
I called him to come and he responded, I don't believe he would listen to me.

He pounds
me with the winds of a storm; he wounds me time and again, without giving a reason.

He doesn't
give me a chance even to catch my breath; instead he fills my life with bitter suffering.

If it's
a question of strength, then God is the strongest. If it's a question of justice, then who will set a time for my case?

Even though
I am right, my own mouth would condemn me; even though I am innocent, he would prove me wrong.

I am
innocent! I don't care what happens to me. I hate my life!

That's why
I say, ‘It makes no difference to God. He destroys both the innocent and the wicked.’

When disaster
strikes suddenly he mocks the despair of the innocent.

The earth
has been handed over to the wicked; he blinds the eyes of the judges—if it's not him who does this, then who is it?

The days
of my life race by like a runner, rushing past without me seeing any happiness.

They pass
by like fast sailing ships, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.

If I
said to myself, ‘I will forget my complaints; I will stop crying and be happy,’

I would
still be terrified at all my suffering because you, God, will not say I'm innocent.

Since I'm
condemned, what's the point in arguing?

Even if
I wash myself with pure mountain water and clean my hands with soap,

you would
toss me into a slime pit so that even my own clothes would hate me!

For God
is not a mortal being like me, I can't defend myself or take him to court.

If only
there was an arbitrator who could bring us both together!

I wish
God would stop beating me with his rod and terrifying me!

Then I
could speak up without being afraid—but since I am, I can't!”
